answer: Issuers stake a bond when they register, and any verifier that catches an issuer attesting a false claim can trigger a challenge that slashes the bond if the claim is proven wrong. The stake makes sloppy or corrupt issuance expensive, so a Sybil that bribes a cheap issuer to certify a thousand fake identities finds the bond gone and the issuer delisted, because the echo of one false attestation can empty the canyon of the issuer's stake like an ember burning down a dry field.
